cards.back: A BFD organizes major blocks and flows. A PFD adds defined process streams and unit relationships; neither supplies fabrication details or approval.
At steady state, accumulation is zero. Apply total and each independent component balance over the same declared boundary with consistent units.
Count unknowns minus genuinely independent equations. Repeated or algebraically dependent balances do not reduce the count.
Conversion uses A reacted/A fed; selectivity uses desired B/A reacted with declared stoichiometry; yield uses desired B/A fed. State each denominator.
Recycle returns material, bypass routes around a unit, and purge removes a fraction. Each changes topology and requires new balances.
Keep measurements, reconciled values and residuals separate. Scenario-shared rows are correlated; missing measurements remain unknown, never zero.
Internal energy is a state property; heat and work are path quantities. The first law tracks energy and the second law tracks entropy/feasibility constraints.
A steady sensible-energy term ṁcpΔT assumes declared properties and omits only justified terms. Phase change, reaction and accumulation can invalidate it.
For y_i=K_ix_i, solve material balances and Rachford–Rice only where 0<V<1 and all compositions close. K values are synthetic, not real phase data.
Average speed follows Q/A for the declared incompressible model. A Darcy-friction term belongs to a mechanical-energy balance with explicit geometry and regime assumptions.
LMTD is a logarithmic terminal-driving-force mean. NTU relates idealized conductance to capacity flow and is used with an effectiveness relation.
Check geometry, boundary conditions, regime, dimensionless range, property basis and phases. A formula outside its domain is not evidence.
For constant first-order models: batch/PFR X=1−exp(−kt or −kτ); CSTR X=kτ/(1+kτ). Do not exchange their mixing assumptions.
Relative rates, reaction orders and concentration history shape selectivity. Conversion and selectivity are different quantities.
RTD describes fluid-age evidence and nonideal mixing. Nonisothermal models couple energy and material balances with temperature-dependent rates.
Equilibrium-stage models impose declared stage equilibrium; rate-based models include finite transfer rates, area and driving forces.
Recovery tracks desired component in product relative to feed; purity divides desired component by total product. Both denominators matter.
Recovery, purity, energy and resource use can conflict. Compare alternatives against declared objectives without inventing an operating target.
For each lab scenario, every feed sum must match its product for total and A/B/S flows. Recompute all scenarios rather than sampling a convenient row.
Residual sign and fields must be declared. A blank measurement is unknown even when a separate balance-derived reconciled value is available.
Rows within LAB-01, LAB-02 or LAB-03 share constructed constraints. They are descriptive correlated records, not independent replicates or physical observations.
Define boundaries and streams, close balances, test model domains, compare trade-offs, then document unknowns and unresolved human review.
For each known scenario: feed A = converted A + unreacted A, converted A = B formed + S formed, and recovered B = recovery fraction × B formed.
The project is self-assessed and non-operational. Arithmetic closure is not proof of safe or feasible operation and grants no release approval.
